Notes

The voice cannot release its words or its attachment, so it builds a perfect elsewhere out of very ordinary wishes.

在嘴边

嘴边 places the words at the edge of the mouth, almost out. The following 说不出 means being unable to get them spoken. That spatial precision matters: the problem is not having nothing to say, but reaching the threshold and stopping. The repeated lines keep the listener at that same threshold with him.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
憋

憋 is keeping something in—breath, words, tears or emotion—under pressure. 默默 adds silence, 一个人 adds being alone, and 很久 adds duration. Those small modifiers make the repeated opening more than a generic inability to speak. In a song called “Numb,” the lyric is crowded with feeling that cannot find a usable exit.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
其实也没什么

“Actually, it’s nothing” follows repeated descriptions of how much the unsaid words hurt. That placement makes it sound like the reflex of minimizing a problem after admitting it. The next line directs blame inward. The contradiction is recognizable conversational behavior: confession can be followed by an immediate attempt to withdraw the importance of what was confessed.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
拧巴

拧巴 is colloquial language for being twisted up, contrary or at odds with oneself. It keeps a tactile image of something that will not straighten out. The surrounding actions explain the knot: he cannot speak, cannot let go and still wants to try. “Tied up in knots” preserves that sense of conflict.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
还不愿意让他走

不愿意 is unwilling, not unable. After several lines about things he cannot do, the wording briefly assigns him agency over the attachment: part of him does not consent to its ending. That makes the knot more difficult than finding the right advice. Understanding that he might eventually think it through does not yet make him want to release it.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
想通

想通 literally reaches a point where thought is open or passes through: arriving at an understanding that lets a problem settle. It contrasts with the twisted 拧巴 and blocked mouth. The lyric gives that opening to “sooner or later,” then returns to what he wants now. A future resolution is imaginable without being emotionally available in the present.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
还有救

还有救 literally leaves open the possibility of rescue; in everyday speech it can mean “there’s hope for me yet.” 说不定, “maybe,” stops that hope from becoming certainty. The phrase follows a decision to try again before he has made sense of what happened. Action therefore briefly gets ahead of understanding rather than waiting for a complete explanation.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
另外一个世界

另外一个世界 introduces an alternate setting where the speaker can be outstanding. The wishes that follow are strikingly conventional: youth, health, happiness and money. The extravagant thing is having them all at once with no remaining worries. The verse gives this complete package to an elsewhere, creating distance between the fantasy and the person still unable to speak here.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
完美的一生

The short list of desirable conditions ends by declaring an entire life perfect. “Ah” gives the summary the flavor of a sigh or a small daydream rather than a practical plan. The gap between the compact, easily stated list and the difficulty of the opening is the point: it is simple to name an ideal life and much harder to inhabit one.

About Jackzebra and this mixtape

Zhuang Zhuang Mixtape arrived on Surf Gang on October 2, 2026: 55 tracks, opening with Sour and closing with Sweet. Its cast widens from YoungQueenz on Poker Face to User116, Effie, kuru, yoyi, 春 and 南部犯罪份子. Aghast has a production credit on every track from Hitman through Snatch, giving that stretch a shared collaborator behind its changing scenes.

Surf Gang release · Artist credits

Jackzebra told AVYSS that he writes while singing over a beat he has listened to repeatedly, keeping the images in his head central. He values the room Mandarin leaves for indirect meanings. Listen for ordinary phrases becoming physical scenes: familiarity becomes cooking, authority becomes family seniority, and a tired saying suddenly turns into a threat.

AVYSS interview, 2024

In STATIC, he describes mixtapes as a format for letting ideas flow, reserving an official debut album for later. In a separate conversation about Above & Beyond, he compared that earlier tape to a collection of his producer friends’ work. The credits here likewise reward attention: long-running collaborators sit alongside guests working in Mandarin, Korean and English.

STATIC interview · Sabukaru interview, 2025

The small details connect to his stated interests: he has described playing Temple Run in transit and before shows, watching Top Boy, and wanting to score White Oleander. These give the songs specific points of contact with his life. The notes follow those connections alongside the lyrics’ jokes, invented scenes and competing voices.

His recommendations in Perfectly Imperfect · Dazed interview, 2025 · Interview questionnaire, 2025

Jackzebra has pushed back on being made to represent all of China’s underground. These notes stay close to the words: what an expression usually means, what changes in this line, and how another song answers it. Cultural references have sources; interpretations rest on details you can hear or read in the song.
